notes: DETECTION vs CONSTRUCTION split: on the two detection evals (1,2) with-skill and baseline BOTH scored 100% — general onion knowledge (helped by the auto-injected CLAUDE.md) already finds planted violations. The skill's whole measurable edge came from eval-3 (construction): 100% vs 33%.

Eval-3 is the discriminating case. Baseline invented a generic domain/application/infrastructure/presentation subfolder tree, fabricated its own GithubWebhookPort + gh.forWorkspace() instead of the real container.github(), and hand-waved the contracts location + module registration. With-skill matched every DevDigest-specific wiring detail.

Assertions 1-6 of eval-1 and 1-5 of eval-2 are NON-DISCRIMINATING (both configs pass) — they confirm the fixtures are catchable but don't measure the skill. Consider hardening future fixtures with subtler, DevDigest-specific-only traps (e.g. db/rows vs db/schema nuance, the type-elision loophole, thin-module grandfathering) to make detection evals discriminate.

Quality gap not captured by pass/fail: with-skill cites exact dependency-cruiser rule names (route-no-direct-db, core-stays-pure, etc.), the known-warn baseline, and the verify command; baseline uses generic vocabulary. Baseline also MISSED the z.infer-duplication issue in eval-2 (called the hand-written interface 'correct').

COST: with-skill is slower/heavier (reads SKILL.md + rule files). Eval-1 with-skill 141s/50k tok vs baseline 137s/32k tok; eval-2 109s/37k vs 73s/26k. ~1.4x tokens for the guidance — worth it on construction, marginal on detection.
